tools.title: Create ad set
tools.description:
Creates a single ad set under an existing campaign in PAUSED state.

 BEFORE CALLING: The `ads_create_campaign` response includes `valid_optimization_goals` and `recommended_optimization_goal` for the campaign's objective. Use ONLY values from that list for `optimization_goal`. That list is per objective only: the server either replaces a goal outside it with the recommended default, or rejects a goal the ad set's `destination_type` and `promoted_object` do not offer and names the goals they do. A goal on the list can still be rejected for its `destination_type`, `promoted_object`, or `billing_event`; follow the pairings on those parameters.

 TARGETING — ADVANTAGE+ AUDIENCE (A+A) DECISION: Meta recommends A+A. Default: omit `targeting_automation`; the server then normally turns A+A on. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

campaign_id.description: The campaign ID to create the ad set under. The campaign must not be DELETED or ARCHIVED; read its status and effective_status with ads_get_ad_entities first.

billing_event.description: What the advertiser is charged for. Use IMPRESSIONS, which is valid for every optimization_goal. Other billing events are goal-specific: for example, LINK_CLICKS pairs with optimization_goal=LINK_CLICKS, THRUPLAY with THRUPLAY, and PAGE_LIKES with PAGE_LIKES. Invalid pairings are rejected. Billing events: APP_INSTALLS, CLICKS, COMPLETED_VIDEO_VIEWS, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, LISTING_INTERACTION, OFFER_CLAIMS, PAGE_LIKES, POST_ENGAGEMENT, PURCHASE, SIX_SECOND_VIDEO_VIEWS, THRUPLAY, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS, VIDEO_VIEWS.

optimization_goal.description:
What the ad set is optimized for. Pick the value whose human label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. Supported values: REACH (Reach), IMPRESSIONS (Impressions), LINK_CLICKS (Link Clicks), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS (Landing Page Views), ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Engaged Page Views — users who stay on the landing page), POST_ENGAGEMENT (Post Engagement), PAGE_LIKES (Page Likes), EVENT_RESPONSES (Event Responses), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (Conversions / Purchases / Add to Cart), VALUE (Conversion Value / ROAS), LEAD_GENERATION (Leads), QUALITY_LEAD (Conversion Leads), CONVERSATIONS (Conversations), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Messaging Purchases — optimize for purchases in messaging conversations; pair with a messaging destination_type such as MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT), QUALITY_CALL (Calls), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Meaningful Calls — optimize for call attempts initiated through messaging), APP_INSTALLS (App Installs), THRUPLAY (ThruPlay), TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS (2-second continuous video plays), VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE (Instagram profile visits — pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE), PROFILE_VISIT (profile visits — pair with destination_type=FACEBOOK_PAGE for "Maximize Facebook Page visits" or destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for IG profile visits), PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT (Profile and Page Engagement — unified profile/page visit optimization; pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE), REMINDERS_SET (Reminders set), AD_RECALL_LIFT (Ad Recall Lift). Some goals are gated per-account (e.g. MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION, MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT, ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS) — the Marketing API returns an error if the account is not eligible. Compatibility with the parent campaign's objective is enforced by the Marketing API. 

  OBJECTIVE → COMPATIBLE optimization_goal VALUES (default listed first; pick from this list based on the parent campaign's objective — values outside the list are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available with this objective"): OUTCOME_AWARENESS → REACH (default), IMPRESSIONS, AD_RECALL_LIFT, THRUPLAY, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS. OUTCOME_TRAFFIC → LINK_CLICKS (default), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, CONVERSATIONS, THRUPLAY, VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, PROFILE_VISIT, QUALITY_CALL, REMINDERS_SET. OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT → THRUPLAY (default), POST_ENGAGEMENT, EVENT_RESPONSES, PAGE_LIKES, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_LEADS → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, VALUE, CONVERSATIONS (destinations that include WhatsApp only), QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_SALES → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), VALUE, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS; with destination_type WEBSITE none is available unless promoted_object has a conversion signal (e.g. pixel_id with custom_event_type, or custom_conversion_id) or a catalog product_set_id, so for link clicks or landing page views without one use OUTCOME_TRAFFIC. OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION → APP_INSTALLS (default), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, REACH, VALUE. VIDEO_VIEWS (10-second views) is deprecated under every objective; use THRUPLAY. Account-gated goals that may also be valid for specific objectives: ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Traffic), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Traffic, Engagement), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Engagement, Sales — messaging destinations only). When in doubt, pick the default (first value listed).

targeting.description: JSON string of targeting spec. IMPORTANT: Do NOT invent interest IDs — interest targeting requires real numeric IDs from the Facebook Targeting Search API (typically 13–16 digit numbers like "6003139266461"). If you do not have valid interest IDs, use geo_locations-only broad targeting instead. Example (broad, recommended when interest IDs are unknown): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]}}. Omit targeting_automation by default (the server normally turns A+A on). Add "targeting_automation":{"advantage_audience":0} only for one of the four advertiser-side reasons in the tool description; never because an earlier ad set had it. Put `targeting_automation`, `excluded_custom_audiences`, `publisher_platforms` and every `*_positions` list inside this object. List custom audience exclusions in `excluded_custom_audiences` as objects with the audience `id`. For Facebook Feed and Instagram Reels only, use {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"publisher_platforms":["facebook","instagram"],"facebook_positions":["feed"],"instagram_positions":["reels"]}. For Advantage+ placements, omit `publisher_platforms` and every `*_positions` field. Example (with verified interest): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"flexible_spec":[{"interests":[{"id":"6003139266461","name":"Movies"}]}]}. Never use placeholder IDs like "000" or "123" — they will be rejected. SPECIAL AD CATEGORIES: when the parent campaign is HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT or FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, give every city, address or custom location a `radius` and `distance_unit` of at least 15 miles (25 km), whatever country is targeted; this meets the minimum in every region. Never use `zips`, `subcities`, `neighborhoods`, `subneighborhoods`, `metro_areas`, `small_geo_areas`, `electoral_districts` or `political_districts` in `geo_locations`. Every country targeted by `geo_locations` must appear in the parent campaign's `special_ad_category_country`; territories of those countries are also allowed. Keep `age_min` at 18 and `age_max` at 65, and do not add interests or other detailed targeting. `countries` and `regions` need no radius.

advantage_audience_off_reason.description: When you send `targeting_automation.advantage_audience` = 0, the advertiser-side reason from the tool description that applies: ADVERTISER_REQUESTED_OFF (1), HARD_AGE_REQUIREMENT (2), CUSTOM_AUDIENCE_ONLY (3) or ADVANTAGE_AUDIENCE_UNAVAILABLE (4).

daily_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Daily budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO (i.e., has no campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget). Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. IMPORTANT: If the user has not explicitly requested ABO, prefer setting campaign_daily_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended). If neither budget is set here and the parent is not CBO, the tool will ask you to choose CBO or ABO explicitly.

lifetime_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Lifetime budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO. Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Requires end_time. Prefer setting campaign_lifetime_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended).

start_time.description: Optional. Ad set start time in ISO 8601 format.

end_time.description: Optional. Ad set end time in ISO 8601 format. Required when this ad set has lifetime_budget, or when its parent campaign has a lifetime budget and no campaign-level schedule (under a scheduled campaign the ad set takes the campaign's stop time).

bid_strategy.description: ABO ONLY — do NOT pass under a CBO parent campaign (one that has campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget set); the campaign's bid strategy applies to all of its ad sets. Optional. Ad set bid strategy. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (default — automatic bidding, no bid_amount needed), LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets a maximum bid cap in cents), COST_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets an average cost-per-result target in cents), LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (for value optimization — requires bid_constraints with roas_average_floor). If omitted, defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid).

bid_amount.description: Bid cap or cost target in cents. Pass it when this ad set's bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP or COST_CAP; LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid) needs none. Under a CBO parent campaign, pass it exactly when the campaign's bid strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP or COST_CAP.

promoted_object.description: REQUIRED when optimization_goal is OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, APP_INSTALLS, PROFILE_VISIT, or PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT. For PROFILE_VISIT and PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT, include page_id: {"page_id":"<PAGE_ID>"}, including when the destination is Instagram only. Optional for other goals (REACH, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, etc.). JSON string of promoted object spec — usually a pixel, app, page, or custom event. REQUIRED for OUTCOME_SALES campaigns with WEBSITE destination: without a conversion signal in promoted_object (e.g. pixel_id with custom_event_type, or custom_conversion_id) or a catalog product_set_id, no optimization goal is valid for that combination and the create fails with "Performance goal isn't available". Strongly recommended for OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS and VALUE under OUTCOME_LEADS as well. A pixel_id needs custom_event_type (or pixel_rule) for every goal, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS included, unless it is an offsite or CRM-ready pixel. For OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, promoted_object is optional except for PROFILE_VISIT. Format examples: {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE"} (website conversions; use an event the campaign objective supports, e.g. PURCHASE for OUTCOME_SALES, LEAD for OUTCOME_LEADS; a pixel_id without custom_event_type is usually rejected), {"custom_conversion_id":"123"} (custom conversion), {"application_id":"123","object_store_url":"..."} (app installs), {"page_id":"123"} (page-related goals; under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT also set destination_type, see that parameter), {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE","custom_attribution_source_ids":["456"]} (Custom Attribution / passback — optimizes toward an external Source-of-Truth attribution source. Requires an OUTCOME_SALES campaign, an OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS or VALUE goal, LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP bidding and a PURCHASE event. Incremental attribution must be disabled, and value_rule_set_id must not be set. Supported promoted object types are PIXEL (website-only), WEB_AND_APP, and PRODUCT_SET; MOBILE_APP (app-only) is not supported. Use one source id for website-only. Up to two are allowed for website+app, or for a catalog product set with both web and app sources: list the web/pixel CAS first and the app CAS second. A single CAS can cover website+app when its pixel dataset already has a linked app. A source id is NOT a pixel or dataset id — it comes from Events Manager > Settings > Custom attribution source. Settable only when the ad set is created).

destination_type.description: REQUIRED for messaging and profile goals — see below. Where the ad drives people. Values: WEBSITE, APP, MESSENGER, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, WHATSAPP, PHONE_CALL, ON_AD, ON_EVENT, ON_PAGE, ON_POST, ON_VIDEO, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE, LEAD_FORM_MESSENGER. REQUIRED pairings: CONVERSATIONS / MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION / MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT → MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT (under OUTCOME_LEADS, CONVERSATIONS needs a destination that includes WhatsApp; MESSENGER there supports only LEAD_GENERATION). Under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT with a promoted_object: POST_ENGAGEMENT → ON_POST, PAGE_LIKES → ON_PAGE, THRUPLAY / TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS → ON_VIDEO; without a destination those goals are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available". VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_VISIT → FACEBOOK_PAGE or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE. WEBSITE is the typical pairing for LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS / OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS / VALUE goals.

adset_schedule.description: Optional. JSON array of day-parting windows; omit to run ads all the time. Each entry has start_minute and end_minute (minutes from midnight, multiples of 60 from 0 to 1440, at least 60 apart) and days (0-6, 0 = Sunday); a window repeats on every listed day. Requires pacing_type ["day_parting"] on the ad set or its parent campaign. Any schedule other than the single all-week window [{"start_minute":0,"end_minute":1440,"days":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]}] also requires a lifetime budget: lifetime_budget with end_time on the ad set, or a lifetime budget on its CBO campaign. Example (9:00-17:00, Monday-Friday): [{"start_minute":540,"end_minute":1020,"days":[1,2,3,4,5]}]

pacing_type.description: Optional. JSON array of pacing types. Values: ["standard"], ["day_parting"], ["no_pacing"]. ["day_parting"] requires adset_schedule, on this ad set or, when the parent campaign uses day_parting, on every ad set under it. If omitted, the parent campaign's pacing applies (standard when the campaign has no budget).

attribution_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of attribution spec for conversion tracking. RECOMMENDED: omit this field unless the advertiser explicitly requests a specific window. Default: 7-day click-through + 1-day view-through when defaulting is enabled and the goal, objective, destination and promoted object support it; otherwise the field is left unset for the Marketing API. Explicit caller windows are preserved and validated by the API. Override example (7-day click only): [{"event_type":"CLICK_THROUGH","window_days":7}]. Valid event_types: CLICK_THROUGH, VIEW_THROUGH, ENGAGED_VIDEO_VIEW.

frequency_control_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of frequency capping specs.

is_dynamic_creative.description: Optional. Set true for a dynamic creative ad set. It holds one ad, whose creative must be a dynamic creative: an inline asset_feed_spec in ads_create_ad, or the creative_id of an existing dynamic creative. ads_create_creative cannot build one.

existing_customer_budget_percentage.description: Optional. Budget percentage for existing customers (Advantage+ shopping).

tune_for_category.description: Optional. Special ad category tuning. Values: HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS.

bid_constraints.description: REQUIRED when this ad set's bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS, and on every ad set under a CBO parent campaign (one that has campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget set) whose bid strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS: each ad set carries its own minimum ROAS. JSON object with a non-null roas_average_floor (minimum ROAS ratio multiplied by 10000, e.g. {"roas_average_floor":20000} = 2.00x). Do not pass it with any other bid strategy, including under a CBO parent with another bid strategy.

optimization_sub_event.description: Optional. Sub-event for optimization (e.g., specific app event).

multi_optimization_goal_weight.description: Optional. Weight for multi-optimization goal. Values: UNDEFINED, BALANCED, PREFER_EVENT.

daily_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum daily spend target in cents.

daily_spend_cap.description: Optional. Daily spend cap in cents.

lifetime_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum lifetime spend target in cents.

lifetime_spend_cap.description: Optional. Lifetime spend cap in cents.

dsa_beneficiary.description: Optional. Digital Services Act beneficiary name.

dsa_payor.description: Optional. Digital Services Act payor name.

campaign_attribution.description: Optional. Attribution type for app campaigns. Values: AEM, SKAN.

is_incremental_attribution_enabled.description: Optional. Whether the campaign should use incremental attribution optimization. Incremental attribution is an attribution model that optimizes ad delivery for incremental conversions. It uses machine learning models that predict whether a conversion is caused by an ad. Supported bid strategies are: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, COST_CAP, and LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (autobid campaigns are always allowed). Supported optimization goals are: OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, and RETURN_ON_AD_SPEND. Supported promoted object types are: PIXEL, WEBSITE, PRODUCT_SET, WEB_AND_APP, and WEB_AND_SHOP (plus WEBSITE_AND_IN_STORE and WEBSITE_APP_AND_IN_STORE for accounts gated into omni/web-app-instore). For value-optimized goals (VALUE, ROAS), the supported promoted object semantic value types are: VALUE, MARGIN, and LIFETIME_VALUE. When using incremental attribution you should not provide a value for `attribution_spec`.

adlabels.description: Optional. JSON array of ad label specs. Example: [{"name":"My Label"}]

budget_schedule_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of budget schedule specs for high demand periods. Each spec has time_start, time_end, budget_value, budget_value_type.

budget_source.description: Optional. Budget source. Values: NONE, RMN.

budget_split_set_id.description: Optional. Budget split set ID as numeric string.

daily_imps.description: Optional. Daily impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

lifetime_imps.description: Optional. Lifetime impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

io_number.description: Optional. Insertion order number for direct deals.

cost_bidding_mode.description: Optional. Cost bidding mode. Values: VOLUME_FOCUSED, BALANCED, COST_FOCUSED.

campaign_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of campaign spec with name, objective, and buying_type for inline campaign creation.

campaign_active_time.description: Optional. Campaign active time as a UNIX timestamp (seconds since epoch).

campaign_targeting_consolidation.description: Optional. Campaign targeting consolidation phase. Values: PHASE_1, PHASE_2, PHASE_3.

source_adset_id.description: Optional. Source ad set ID to copy from, as numeric string.

split_test_config_splits_index.description: Optional. Index for the splits vector from split test config on the parent campaign.

automatic_manual_state.description: Optional. Automatic/manual state. Values: UNSET, AUTOMATIC, MANUAL.

calling_settings.description: Optional. JSON object of calling settings for call-based ads.

naming_template_custom_fields.description: Optional. JSON object of naming template custom fields for ad set naming conventions.

marketing_goal.description: Optional. Marketing goal. Values: NONE, NEW_CUSTOMER_ACQUISITION.

biz_ai_enabled_state.description: Optional. Business AI enabled state. Values: APP_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED, APP_ONBOARDING_STARTED, APP_ONBOARDING_NOT_REQUIRED, OPT_OUT_ONBOARDING, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_ON, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_OFF, NOT_ENABLED, CURRENT_CAMPAIGN_ONLY, ALL_CAMPAIGNS.

saved_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of saved audience spec including targeting, name, and other audience configuration.

saved_audience_id.description: Optional. Saved audience ID as numeric string.

targeting_as_signal.description: Optional. Indicates if campaign is using targeting criteria as a signal.

adjust_lookalikes.description: Optional. Whether to adjust lookalike audiences.

brand_audience_id.description: Optional. Brand audience ID as numeric string.

reporting_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of reporting audience spec for cross-account reporting.

placement.description: Optional advanced placement spec. For ordinary manual placement selection, use `publisher_platforms` and the matching `*_positions` fields inside `targeting`; do not send the same restriction in both fields.

placement_soft_opt_out.description: Optional. JSON object of placement soft opt-out spec to exclude specific placements without hard constraints.

rf_prediction_id.description: Optional. Reach and frequency prediction ID as numeric string.

contextual_bundling_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of contextual bundling spec for ads in Facebook contextual surfaces.

creative_sequence.description: Optional. JSON array of ad group IDs defining the sequence to show to users.

creative_diversity_data.description: Optional. JSON object of creative diversity data including scores and labels for creative variation analysis.

creative_diversity_label.description: Optional. Creative diversity label. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

creative_diversity_score.description: Optional. Creative diversity score (0.0-1.0) measuring variation across ad creatives.

creative_fatigue_prediction_ple.description: Optional. JSON object of creative fatigue prediction PLE data.

is_dynamic_creative_format_automation.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative format automation.

is_dynamic_creative_optimization.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative optimization. Deprecated in v3.2.

multi_event_conversion_attribution_windo.description: Optional. Multi-event conversion attribution window in seconds.

low_creative_reach.description: Optional. Low creative reach indicator. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

conversion_goal_id.description: Optional. ID of the conversion goal (CSA) as numeric string.

conversion_locations.description: Optional; usually omit, since destination_type already sets where conversions happen. Common values: WEBSITE, MOBILE_APP, WEB_AND_APP, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, PHONE_CALL, WEBSITE_AND_PHONE_CALL.

conversion_value_expression_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of conversion value expression specs.

partnership_ad_content_lists.description: Optional. JSON array of partnership ad content lists.

shops_ads_metadata_tags.description: Optional. JSON array of shops ads metadata tag integers.

is_message_marketing.description: Optional. Whether this is message marketing.

time_based_ad_rotation_id_blocks.description: Optional. JSON array of arrays of ad group IDs for time-based ad rotation.

time_based_ad_rotation_intervals.description: Optional. JSON array of UNIX timestamps defining date ranges for ad rotation.

time_start.description: Optional. Time start in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_stop.description: Optional. Time stop in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_suggestion.description: Optional. JSON object of suggested start/stop time for the ad set based on delivery optimization.

include_in_ad_study_cell_id.description: Optional. Ad study cell ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

include_in_ad_study_id.description: Optional. Ad study ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

lightweight_split_test_options.description: Optional. JSON object of lightweight A/B split test configuration options.

guidance_lift_estimate.description: Optional. JSON object of lift estimation for each guidance object.

brand_safety_config.description: Optional. JSON object of brand safety configuration.

breakdown_effect_eligibility.description: Optional. Whether breakdown effect is eligible.

is_lifetime_flex_with_valid_schedule.description: Optional. Whether the campaign is lifetime flex with a valid schedule.

is_sac_cfca_terms_certified.description: Optional. Whether SAC CFCA terms are certified.

metrics_metadata.description: Optional. JSON object of metrics metadata related to this ad set.

relative_value.description: Optional. Relative value weight (0.0-1.0) for multi-optimization goal balancing.

value_rule_set_id.description: Optional. Value rule set ID as numeric string.

value_rules_applied.description: Optional. Whether value rules are applied.

value_rules_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of value rules spec.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true to avoid showing too many UI widgets: when creating many ad objects at once, when creating multiple levels together for the same goal (e.g. a campaign, ad set and ad in one flow), or when the user asks to hide the UI.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

tools.title: Create campaign
tools.description:
Creates a single campaign (campaign group) in PAUSED state. Use this to create just a campaign without an ad set or ad. 

 BUDGET PLACEMENT — DEFAULT TO CBO: Unless the advertiser explicitly requests ad-set-level budgeting (ABO), put their stated budget at campaign level (CBO). CBO controls where the budget is allocated; it does not determine the amount or cadence. 

 BUDGET AMOUNT AND CADENCE — DO NOT INFER: Set campaign_daily_budget only when the advertiser states a daily amount, and campaign_lifetime_budget only when they state a total campaign budget. Pass every budget value in the ad account currency's smallest unit (for example, cents for USD). A periodic amount such as "$2,000/month" is neither. If the amount or cadence is unclear, ask and wait before calling this tool; do not stage an assumed value for confirmation. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

objective.description: Campaign objective. Only ODAX outcome values are accepted: OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Legacy objectives (APP_INSTALLS, BRAND_AWARENESS, REACH, LEAD_GENERATION, LINK_CLICKS, VIDEO_VIEWS, etc.) are not supported and the request fails with VALIDATION. Map APP_INSTALLS to OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION.

buying_type.description: Campaign buying type. Values: AUCTION (default), RESERVED.

special_ad_categories.description: JSON array of special ad categories. Defaults to "[]". Values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS, ONLINE_GAMBLING_AND_GAMING. HOUSING also covers mortgages and other home loans. CREDIT is retired: use FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES for other credit, loans, insurance and financial products. Use these exact values, not display names.

campaign_bid_strategy.description: CBO ONLY. Campaign-level bid strategy. Defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP if omitted (recommended for "highest volume" or "lowest cost" strategies). Set explicitly for other strategies. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS. LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS takes its minimum ROAS from each ad set: pass bid_constraints with roas_average_floor on every ads_create_ad_set call under this campaign. Do NOT set this field for ABO — set the bid strategy on the ad set instead.

campaign_daily_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign daily budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_lifetime_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass daily_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

campaign_lifetime_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign lifetime budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_daily_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass lifetime_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

promoted_object.description: Optional. JSON string of promoted object spec. Required for some objectives (APP_PROMOTION, LEADS, etc.). Use product_catalog_id to select a campaign catalog. This does not select product media for ads; choose media at the ad level. A published campaign catalog cannot be removed or replaced.

tools.title: Create creative
tools.description:
## Click-to-messaging creatives (CTWA / CTM / CTD):
Messaging ads send people who click an ad directly into a conversation with the business in Messenger, Instagram Direct, or WhatsApp.

For this tool's single-image, single-video, static-carousel, and existing Instagram-post creatives, use the CTA/link pairs below. Existing-post requirements still apply.

**Always provide `link_url` for single-destination messaging** using the corresponding standard surface link:

| Destination | `call_to_action_type` | `link_url` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WhatsApp (CTWA) | `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE` | `https://api.whatsapp.com/send` |
| Messenger (CTM) | `MESSAGE_PAGE` | `https://fb.com/messenger_doc/` |
| Instagram Direct (CTD) | `INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE` | `https://www.instagram.com/` |

- Match the ad set's `destination_type` to `WHATSAPP`, `MESSENGER`, or `INSTAGRAM_DIRECT` respectively. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: Parent ad account ID, numeric (e.g. "123456789").

page_id.description: Facebook Page ID that will own the creative post. Required for every format except instagram_partnership_ad. For an Instagram Partnership Ad, omit this field and the tool derives the creator's Page-compatible ads identity (its linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page); if provided, it must match that identity. For a Facebook Partnership Ad, set it to the Page publishing the ad. Must be a Page ID: if the owner is a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, use their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID. If the creative is for a PROFILE_VISIT or PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT ad set, set page_id to that ad set's promoted_object.page_id; read it with ads_get_ad_entities first.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image asset. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_hash inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

image_url.description: URL of an image. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_url inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account. Required for a single-video ad, but not sufficient by itself: also provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url as the video thumbnail / cover image. For PAC or MMU, put video_id inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

product_set_id.description: ID of a product set from the advertiser's catalog. Required for Advantage+ catalog carousel ads. When provided, creates a carousel creative that dynamically populates card content from the catalog at delivery time. Do not provide image_hash, image_url, or video_id when using product_set_id.

product_extensions_product_set_id.description: Product set to feature in Product Extensions (from ads_catalog_list_product_sets). Only applies when product_extensions is opted in; omit it to use the recommended set. Different from product_set_id, which creates a catalog carousel.

objective.description: Objective of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with conversion_location and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected when the tool runs the Product Extensions checks. Only these two objectives are eligible for Product Extensions; a campaign on any other objective cannot use it. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

conversion_location.description: Conversion location of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with objective and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected when the tool runs the Product Extensions checks. Pair PIXEL with objective OUTCOME_SALES, or WEBSITE with OUTCOME_TRAFFIC; no other pairing is eligible. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

link_url.description: Destination URL the creative clicks to (e.g. "https://example.com/landing"). Required for image ads, catalog carousel ads, and PAC or MMU containing an image, unless messaging_destination_type is set, which rejects link_url; optional for single-video, video-only PAC, and video-only MMU. Always include https:// scheme; if omitted the tool prepends it automatically. For catalog carousel ads, this is the default landing URL; product-specific deep links from the catalog may override it at delivery time.

display_link.description: Short URL or domain displayed on the ad (e.g. "Verizon.com"). This is presentation text, not the destination URL; put the click destination in link_url. Must be URL-shaped — a bare domain is fine, arbitrary text like "Shop now" is rejected. Supported for image, single-video, PAC, MMU, static-carousel, and Advantage+ catalog-carousel creatives. link_url is required when display_link is provided. Immutable after the creative is published. The link line that shows it is being removed from Facebook mobile Feed for single-image and single-video ads, so it may not be visible there; the response carries a warning when that applies.

message.description: One body/primary-text value shown above the image, video, or carousel. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use primary_texts instead when you want multiple variants. For carousel ads, may contain template strings like {{product.name}} filled from the catalog at delivery time.

primary_texts.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 body/primary-text variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with message; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main text. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use message. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

description.description: One short description value. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use descriptions instead when you want multiple variants. Maps to link_data.description for image ads, video_data.link_description for video ads, or template_data.description for carousel ads. Facebook Feed does not display it on single-image or single-video ads and Instagram has no description line; the response carries a warning when that applies. For video ads, also provide link_url when you set description.

descriptions.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 short-description variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with description; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main description, so the description rules apply: on a single-video ad, also provide link_url. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use description. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

call_to_action_type.description: Call-to-action button type. Defaults to LEARN_MORE if omitted. Must be an exact UPPER_CASE value from the backend CTA enum — do NOT invent or reformat a value, or the request is rejected with "call_to_action[type] must be one of the following values: …". Use one of the accepted values below; pick the one whose label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. CTA destination is auto-set to link_url. With source_instagram_media_id, every value except NO_BUTTON requires link_url. Telephone CTAs (CALL, CALL_NOW, CALL_ME, MISSED_CALL) are not supported because they require a tel: destination, which this tool cannot supply. Use a supported CTA such as CONTACT_US, or create the telephone CTA in Ads Manager. Accepted values by category: — Shopping: SHOP_NOW (Shop Now), BUY_NOW (Buy Now), ORDER_NOW (Order Now), START_ORDER (Start Order), ADD_TO_CART (Add to Cart), SEE_SHOP (See Shop), BROWSE_SHOP (Browse Shop), VIEW_PRODUCT (View Product), BUY (Buy), SELL_NOW (Sell Now), SHOP_WITH_AI (Shop with AI). — General: LEARN_MORE (Learn More), SIGN_UP (Sign Up), OPEN_LINK (Open Link), GET_STARTED (Get Started), SEE_MORE (See More), FIND_OUT_MORE (Find Out More), VISIT_WEBSITE (Visit Website), GET_DETAILS (Get Details), CONFIRM (Confirm), NO_BUTTON (No Button). — Contact: CONTACT_US (Contact Us), CONTACT (Contact), GET_QUOTE (Get Quote), GET_A_QUOTE (Get a Quote), MESSAGE_PAGE (Message Page), WHATSAPP_MESSAGE (WhatsApp Message), INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE (Instagram Message), GET_IN_TOUCH (Get in Touch), AUDIO_CALL (Audio Call), VIDEO_CALL (Video Call), EMAIL_NOW (Email Now), ASK_A_QUESTION (Ask a Question), CHAT_NOW (Chat Now), CHAT_WITH_US (Chat with Us), ASK_FOR_MORE_INFO (Ask for More Info). — Booking: BOOK_NOW (Book Now), BOOK_TRAVEL (Book Travel), REQUEST_TIME (Request Time), MAKE_AN_APPOINTMENT (Make an Appointment), BOOK_A_CONSULTATION (Book a Consultation), GET_SHOWTIMES (Get Showtimes), BUY_TICKETS (Buy Tickets). — App: INSTALL_APP (Install App), INSTALL_MOBILE_APP (Install Mobile App), USE_APP (Use App), USE_MOBILE_APP (Use Mobile App), DOWNLOAD (Download), PLAY_GAME (Play Game), OPEN_INSTANT_APP (Open Instant App), UPDATE_APP (Update App). — Lead Gen: APPLY_NOW (Apply Now), INQUIRE_NOW (Inquire Now), GET_OFFER (Get Offer), GET_DIRECTIONS (Get Directions). — Engagement: SUBSCRIBE (Subscribe), FOLLOW_PAGE (Follow Page), EVENT_RSVP (RSVP), DONATE (Donate), DONATE_NOW (Donate Now), RAISE_MONEY (Raise Money), REFER_FRIENDS (Refer Friends). — Media: WATCH_VIDEO (Watch Video), WATCH_MORE (Watch More), LISTEN_NOW (Listen Now), LISTEN_MUSIC (Listen Music), WATCH_LIVE_VIDEO (Watch Live Video).

name.description: Name of this ad creative as seen in the ad account's library. Strongly recommended.

headline.description: One short headline shown under the image (link_data.name), video (video_data.title), or carousel cards (template_data.name). Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use headlines instead when you want multiple variants.

headlines.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 headline variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with headline; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main headline. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use headline. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

instagram_user_id.description: Instagram User (IG Business Account) ID for IG placement delivery. For instagram_partnership_ad this is required and identifies the creator; it accepts a numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL, resolves it to a professional account, and derives page_id from the creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page. With source_instagram_media_id this is required and names the account that owns the post. For other formats, pass the numeric id returned by ads_get_ig_accounts or instagram_user_id from an existing valid ad; it is required when the ad will deliver on Instagram placements, including Advantage+ placements.

url_tags.description: URL parameters appended to every destination link of the creative, as a query string without a leading "?", for example "utm_source=meta&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign={{campaign.name}}". Ads Manager calls this URL parameters. Set it here when the advertiser tracks clicks; it cannot be added after the creative is created. Enabled per calling app while it rolls out; where it is not, the request is rejected and nothing is created (see URL parameters and instant forms in the tool description).

lead_gen_form_id.description: ID of an existing instant form (lead form) owned by page_id. The button then opens that form instead of a website, for an ad set that optimizes for leads on the ad (OUTCOME_LEADS campaign, destination_type ON_AD). Single-image and single-video creatives only, and not with messaging_destination_type. call_to_action_type must be one that can open a form: LEARN_MORE (the default when omitted), SIGN_UP, APPLY_NOW, GET_QUOTE, GET_OFFER, SUBSCRIBE, DOWNLOAD, CONTACT, GET_IN_TOUCH or BOOK_TRAVEL; any other value is rejected. link_url is optional here; when omitted, the tool uses the placeholder link Ads Manager uses for instant-form ads. The Page must have accepted the Lead Ads Terms of Service. Enabled per calling app while it rolls out; where it is not, the request is rejected and nothing is created (see URL parameters and instant forms in the tool description).

self_ai_disclosure.description: AI-generated content disclosure for the creative. Set to "OPT_IN" to declare that this creative contains media created or edited with a third-party generative AI tool; set to "OPT_OUT" to declare it does not. Omit if unknown. Only these two exact UPPER_CASE values are accepted. When you opt in, Meta may display an "AI info" label on the ad; whether it appears depends on the regions the ad is delivered to and their AI-transparency requirements. Decide this before creating the creative — no update tool can set it afterwards. Always list this field for the advertiser so they can decide; disclosure is their responsibility, so never set or infer a value on their behalf. The declaration takes effect only where AI-transparency rules require it — currently the European Region, India, Taiwan, California, and New York.

object_story_id.description: ID of an existing organic Page post to boost, as {page_id}_{post_id} (e.g. "1234567890_9876543210"). The embedded page must match page_id. Both halves must be canonical IDs: {page_id} is a Page ID (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, their delegate Page ID — not their profile ID), and {post_id} is the post's own ID — not the ID of a photo, video, or other attachment on it. The post must still exist, be published, belong to that Page, and be visible/promotable by the caller; retrying a deleted, unpublished, or inaccessible post cannot repair it. For an ad set optimized for link clicks, the post must already contain a valid external destination and CTA because existing-post copy and CTA cannot be added here. The post media and copy are used as-is, so do NOT combine this with image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, product_set_id, cards, link_url, message, primary_texts, description, descriptions, headline, headlines, call_to_action_type, or display_link. instagram_user_id may be provided for Instagram placement delivery.

source_instagram_media_id.description: Media ID of an existing organic Instagram post to promote: an id returned by ads_get_ig_media for the account in instagram_user_id, which is required alongside it. page_id must be the Facebook Page linked to that account. Ad media, such as a boosted copy or the effective Instagram media ID read from an existing creative, is rejected. The post media and caption are used as-is, so do NOT combine this with object_story_id, image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, multi_media, product_set_id, cards, message, primary_texts, description, descriptions, headline, headlines, display_link, or a Partnership Ad. link_url optionally adds a button; call_to_action_type picks its label. Every call_to_action_type other than NO_BUTTON requires link_url. Without a link, use NO_BUTTON or omit call_to_action_type.

advantage_plus_creative.description: Turn on Advantage+ Creative — Meta's automatic per-impression creative optimizations (image brightness/contrast, text improvements, and similar). This is the master toggle most callers want. Set true to enable it. Set false to leave the master feature off; false does not override a supplied degrees_of_freedom_spec, and does not turn off the default enhancements; use advantage_plus_creative_defaults=OFF for that. Only set true when the advertiser wants Meta to automatically optimize the creative.

advantage_plus_creative_features.description: Specific Advantage+ Creative feature names to opt the creative into individually. Each entry must be an exact lower_snake_case feature name (e.g. "image_touchups", "text_optimizations", "image_animation"). Most callers only need advantage_plus_creative; use this only when the advertiser asks for specific enhancements.

degrees_of_freedom_spec.description: Raw Marketing API degrees_of_freedom_spec, passed as a JSON-ENCODED STRING (NOT a nested JSON object) — e.g. "{\"creative_features_spec\":{\"text_optimizations\":{\"enroll_status\":\"OPT_OUT\"}}}". Use only for what the advantage_plus_creative / advantage_plus_creative_features shortcuts cannot express: opting a feature OUT, or per-feature customizations. Do not combine it with advantage_plus_creative=true or a non-empty advantage_plus_creative_features list. It may be combined with advantage_plus_creative=false while preserving the raw spec. standard_enhancements is retired: OPT_OUT is ignored and OPT_IN is rejected; set individual features instead.

cards.description: Cards for a STATIC carousel ad (2–10). Distinct from Advantage+ catalog carousel: do NOT combine cards with product_set_id, image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, or multi_media. Each card needs exactly one image (image_hash or image_url); a video card sets video_id and may omit the image, in which case the video's default thumbnail is used. Top-level link_url and call_to_action_type act as per-card fallbacks.

items.description: A single static carousel card.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

image_url.description: URL of the image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video for this card (makes it a video card). A thumbnail is optional: if you omit image_hash/image_url, the video's default thumbnail is used automatically.

link.description: Destination URL for this card. Falls back to the top-level link_url when omitted; https:// is prepended if missing. Required for image cards (via card link or the top-level fallback); optional for video cards.

headline.description: Short headline shown on this card (child_attachments.name). Alias: name.

name.description: Alias for headline (matches ads_get_creatives output). Used only when headline is not set.

description.description: Description text shown on this card (child_attachments.description).

call_to_action_type.description: Per-card CTA button type (same accepted values as the top-level call_to_action_type). Falls back to the top-level call_to_action_type.

placement_customizations.description: Placement Asset Customization (2–10 assets). Each entry contains exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id. Exactly one entry is the fallback and contains no placement fields. Other entries need non-empty publisher_platforms; placement rules and media assets may not repeat or overlap. When one asset serves multiple platforms, combine those platforms and their positions in one entry instead of repeating the asset in separate entries. Never reuse an override asset as the fallback. If the request has no fallback, ask for one and do not call the tool. Do not combine with multi_media, placement_videos, or top-level media fields.

items.description: One image or video and the non-overlapping placements where it should be used.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed (ready). Provide exactly one media field.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this asset: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback asset.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

multi_media.description: Multi-media optimization (MMU) asset pool with 2–10 unique images, videos, or both. Meta chooses which eligible asset to deliver. Pair it with primary_texts, headlines, and descriptions for up to five variants of each; use the singular message, headline, and description fields only when you want one value. This field does not set exact placement rules or a fallback; use placement_customizations for that. Do not combine with placement_customizations, placement_videos, top-level media, product_set_id, cards, object_story_id, or facebook_partnership_ad.

items.description: One image or video in the delivery-optimized MMU asset pool.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed. The tool uses its default thumbnail. Provide exactly one media field.

placement_videos.description: Legacy video-only Placement Asset Customization input (2–10). New calls should use placement_customizations. Exactly one entry must be a fallback that contains only video_id. Other entries require non-empty publisher_platforms. Rules and videos may not repeat or overlap. Do not combine with placement_customizations, multi_media, or top-level media fields.

items.description: A pre-uploaded video and the placements where it should be used.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this video: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback video.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

facebook_partnership_ad.description: Facebook Partnership Ad (branded content) created from an existing post — via an ad code (facebook_boost_post_access_token) or by referencing the post directly (object_story_id). Provide this object to create a Partnership Ad — do NOT also provide image_hash, image_url, video_id, multi_media, product_set_id, or cards. To build a new Instagram Partnership Ad creative from media instead, use instagram_partnership_ad; to boost a creator's existing Instagram post, use ads_boost_ig_post.

facebook_boost_post_access_token.description: Encrypted ad code (a.k.a. "boost post access token") that a Facebook creator generated to authorize this advertiser to boost one of the creator's existing Facebook posts as a Facebook Partnership Ad. Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

object_story_id.description: Reference to an existing Facebook branded-content post to boost, formatted "<post_owner_page_id>_<post_id>". The page half is the Page ID of the post's owner (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus owner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID); the post half must be the post's own ID, not the ID of an attachment on it. Use when the advertiser already has permission on the post (instead of an ad code). Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

ad_format.description: Partnership Ad header format, as an integer. Optional; omit it unless the advertiser asked for a specific header, in which case: 1 = dual header (both identities, the default), 2 = single header, 3 = dynamic (optimized at delivery).

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the Partnership Ad's secondary identity (the boosted post's owner is the primary). In a sponsor boost it is the Page publishing the ad, the same value as page_id; in a creator boost it is the partner Page. Must be a Page ID — for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus partner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID.

instagram_partnership_ad.description: Instagram Partnership Ad (branded content) built from new media in this same call. Unlike facebook_partnership_ad, this one DOES carry media — supply image_hash, image_url, video_id or cards as usual. Set instagram_user_id to the CREATOR's numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL; page_id is derived from the resolved creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page unless that matching identity ID is provided. The two fields here name the sponsoring brand. To promote a post the creator has already published, use ads_boost_ig_post instead — this object is for a new creative only, and cannot be combined with object_story_id.

sponsor_instagram_user_id.description: REQUIRED. Instagram account ID of the sponsoring brand. This is what distinguishes an Instagram Partnership Ad from a Facebook one, so it must be the brand and never the creator — the creator goes in the top-level instagram_user_id.

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the same sponsoring brand. Both sponsor fields are required together: supplying only one leaves the brand half-identified and the ad would be created as an ordinary one.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

tools.title: Create custom audience
tools.description:
Creates a custom audience under an ad account. Supported subtypes are CUSTOM
(customer list), WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, MOBILE_APP, and LOOKALIKE.

## When to use

Use this tool only to create a new custom audience.

- Customer-list membership changes are not supported by Ads MCP. Use Ads
 Manager > Audiences.
- Use ads_update_custom_audience to modify an existing audience.
- Use ads_delete_custom_audience to delete an audience.

## Ads Manager guidance

To add users to an existing customer-list custom audience:

1. Go to Audiences in Ads Manager.
2. Select the customer-list audience, select Edit, then choose Add customers.
 Replace customers and Remove customers are also available.
3. Upload a file or paste the updated list. Include identifiers such as email
 or phone number and, for a value-based list, the customer-value column.
4. Select Next and map the identifiers. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

subtype.description: The type of custom audience to create. Values: CUSTOM (customer list / DFCA — requires customer_file_source), WEBSITE (WCA — requires rule with pixel event_sources), ENGAGEMENT (ECA — requires rule with ig_business/page/shopping_page/shopping_ig/marketplace_listings/lead/ig_lead_generation/canvas event_sources), MOBILE_APP (MACA — requires rule with app event_sources), LOOKALIKE (LAL — requires origin_audience_id and lookalike_ratio; origin must NOT itself be a LOOKALIKE).

origin_audience_id.description: Required for LOOKALIKE subtype only. The numeric ID of an existing custom audience to model this lookalike on, passed as a string. The origin can be CUSTOM (DFCA), WEBSITE (WCA), ENGAGEMENT (ECA), or MOBILE_APP (MACA), but NOT another LOOKALIKE. Ignored for non-LOOKALIKE subtypes.

lookalike_ratio.description: Required for LOOKALIKE subtype only. The share of the population to match. Range: 0.01 (1%, closest match, smallest audience) to 0.20 (20%, broadest, largest audience). Default: 0.01 (1%). Ignored for non-LOOKALIKE subtypes. DO NOT ask the user for a country — geography is handled automatically (allow_international_seeds=true).

customer_file_source.description: Required for CUSTOM subtype only. How the customer data was sourced. Values: USER_PROVIDED_ONLY (advertiser collected directly), PARTNER_PROVIDED_ONLY (from a partner), BOTH_USER_AND_PARTNER_PROVIDED (mixed sources). Ignored for WEBSITE subtype.

rule.description: Required for WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, and MOBILE_APP subtypes. MUST be a JSON-encoded string, NOT a raw JSON object. Pass the rule as a single string value like "{\"inclusions\":{...}}", not as a nested object. Top-level structure: {"inclusions":{...}, "exclusions":{...}}. "exclusions" is optional. Each block has: {"operator":"or","rules":[<rule1>, <rule2>, ...]}. Each rule has: {"event_sources":[{"type":"<TYPE>","id":"<ID>"}], "retention_seconds":<SECONDS>, "filter":{"operator":"and","filters":[...]}, "template":"<TEMPLATE>"}. For WEBSITE: event_sources type must be "pixel". Template is REQUIRED. Three targeting flows: (1) All visitors: template "ALL_VISITORS", filter {"field":"url","operator":"i_contains","value":""} (empty value matches all). tools.description:
Create a short-lived URL for uploading one image or video file for use in ads. Use it for any file you can read yourself: files in your sandbox or workspace, and files from Google Drive, Canva, Dropbox or similar that you download first.  Send every header in upload_headers exactly as returned; do not re-encode or change them. Use --data-binary, not -d or -F. Images can be up to 30 MiB and videos up to 100 MiB. Upload images or videos to an advertiser's ad account from either a local device or a publicly accessible URL. This is the preferred media upload tool for ads. It does not add media to catalog products; use ads_catalog_update_product for product videos.

 ## Local files
 - Set `upload_source` to `LOCAL_FILE` only when the client supports interactive MCP Apps.
 - If the client does not support interactive MCP Apps, use `URL` with `media_type` and a direct, publicly accessible `media_url` instead.
 - Local uploads support JPEG, PNG, GIF, MP4, and MOV/QuickTime files.
 - For a local video, use `LOCAL_FILE`; do not require the user to provide a public URL or set `media_type`.
 - The tool opens the upload app so the user can choose a file from their device.
 - `media_type`, `media_url`, and `name` are ignored for local uploads.

 ## Public URLs
 - Set `upload_source` to `URL`. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

tools.title: Delete custom audience
tools.description:
Permanently deletes a custom audience by its ID.

 ## When to use:
 - Call this tool when the user explicitly asks to delete or remove a custom audience.
 - Use when cleaning up unused or outdated audiences.

 ## When NOT to use:
 - Do NOT use to remove people from a customer-list audience. Ads MCP does not support membership changes; use Ads Manager > Audiences, open the audience, and manage its customer list there.
 - Do NOT use to pause or deactivate an audience — deletion is permanent and irreversible.
 - Do NOT use on audiences that have active lookalike audiences derived from them — delete the lookalikes first.
 - Do NOT use on system-managed audiences — only user-created custom audiences can be deleted.

 ## CRITICAL:
 - Deletion is PERMANENT and cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

tools.description:
Create an A/B test (split test). Supports campaign-level (L3), ad-set-level (L2), and creative-level (L1) tests. At least 2 cells are required; the maximum depends on the test type and ad account eligibility. Provide exactly one ad entity ID in each cell. The test runs for a specified duration.

 Each cell is one variant and must contain one ID at the same entity level, from the same ad account. For example: `[{"name":"Control","ad_entity_ids":["120000000000001"]},{"name":"New creative","ad_entity_ids":["120000000000002"]}]`. These are campaign, ad set, or ad IDs—not study IDs or the `act_...` ad account ID. Use `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, such as `2030-01-15`; do not send Unix timestamps.

 KPIs: the primary KPI defaults to cost_per_result and determines the test winner. To use a different primary KPI, pass `primary_kpi` using a supported canonical value. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID (e.g. "act_123456789").

cells.description: Test cells, with exactly one ad entity ID in each cell. Example: [{"name":"Control","ad_entity_ids":["120000000000001"]},{"name":"New creative","ad_entity_ids":["120000000000002"]}]. All IDs must be the same type and belong to the supplied ad account. Use campaign, ad set, or ad IDs here—not study IDs or the ad account ID. At least 2 cells are required; the maximum depends on the test type and ad account eligibility.

items.description: A single test cell.

ad_entity_ids.description: The single ad entity ID for this cell. Provide exactly one ID.

items.description: Ad entity ID (numeric).

test_name.description: Optional name for the test study.

start_time.description: Optional start date as a YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. "2030-01-15"), not a Unix timestamp or date-time. The test starts at midnight in the ad account timezone. The earliest allowed date is tomorrow in that timezone. Defaults to tomorrow.

end_time.description: Optional end date as a YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. "2030-01-22"), not a Unix timestamp or date-time. It must be after start_time and is interpreted at midnight in the ad account timezone. Defaults to 7 days from start.

primary_kpi.description: Optional primary KPI (success metric) for the test. The primary KPI determines the test winner. Omit to default to cost_per_result. Use a supported canonical value. Other action types and custom conversion IDs are not supported. Supported values: catalog_segment_actions:omni_add_to_cart, catalog_segment_actions:omni_purchase, catalog_segment_actions:omni_view_content, catalog_segment_value_omni_purchase_roas:omni_purchase, cost_per_action_type:add_payment_info, cost_per_action_type:add_to_wishlist, cost_per_action_type:app_custom_event.fb_mobile_d2_retention, cost_per_action_type:app_custom_event.fb_mobile_d7_retention, cost_per_action_type:landing_page_view, cost_per_action_type:lead, cost_per_action_type:like, cost_per_action_type:link_click, cost_per_action_type:offline_conversion.other, cost_per_action_type:omni_achievement_unlocked, cost_per_action_type:omni_activate_app, cost_per_action_type:omni_add_to_cart, cost_per_action_type:omni_app_install, cost_per_action_type:omni_complete_registration, cost_per_action_type:omni_custom, cost_per_action_type:omni_initiated_checkout, cost_per_action_type:omni_landing_page_view, cost_per_action_type:omni_level_achieved, cost_per_action_type:omni_purchase, cost_per_action_type:omni_rate, cost_per_action_type:omni_search, cost_per_action_type:omni_spend_credits, cost_per_action_type:omni_tutorial_completion, cost_per_action_type:omni_view_content, cost_per_action_type:onsite_conversion.engaged_page_view, cost_per_action_type:onsite_conversion.messaging_first_reply, cost_per_action_type:post_engagement, cost_per_action_type:rsvp, cost_per_action_type:video_view, cost_per_estimated_ad_recallers, cost_per_result, cpp.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

tools.title: Experiment A/B test get test
tools.description:
Read one A/B test (split test) by an established study_id: name, status/type, schedule, cells/assigned entities, objectives and winner/high performers. Use for a known study or to confirm its configuration after creation. A/B tests compare one variable (creative, audience or placement); judge the winner against the advertiser's actual objective and business-outcome metrics, not just CPM. Mirror their preferred A/B/split-test terminology.

 study_id must be known as an A/B study ID, e.g. from ads_experiment_list_tests or ads_experiment_abtest_create_test. A bare numeric ID, even "show the A/B test for ID123", does not establish its type: ask where it came from or request the Ads Manager URL; do not guess or call this tool. Never pass account/campaign/ad-set/ad IDs as study_id. Shortened; describing this tool returns Meta's full guidance.

tools.title: Experiment A/B test update test
tools.description:
Edits or cancels a running A/B test by study ID. Only the study ID and action are required—the ad account is resolved automatically.

 **ID ROUTING:** `study_id` must be a known A/B test study ID, such as one returned by `ads_experiment_list_tests` or `ads_experiment_abtest_create_test`. A bare numeric ID is not enough evidence that it is a study ID. Never pass an ad account, campaign, ad set, or ad ID. If the user provides an ID with an `act_` prefix, call `ads_experiment_list_tests` with `ad_account_id`; if the conversation identifies it as a campaign, ad set, or ad ID, call that tool with `ad_entity_id`. If the ID type is unknown, ask where the user copied it from or request the Ads Manager URL; do not guess. For date updates, use `YYYY-MM-DD`, such as `2030-01-15`, rather than a Unix timestamp.

 **Supported actions:**
 - "cancel" stops the test with no results preserved. Shortened; load the Meta Ads playbook Skill for Meta's full rules before calling.

ad_account_id.description: Do not ask the user for this. Automatically inferred from the study. Only provide if already known.

study_id.description: The A/B test study ID to edit, typically returned by `ads_experiment_list_tests` or `ads_experiment_abtest_create_test`. A bare numeric ID is not enough evidence that it is a study ID. Do not pass an ad account, campaign, ad set, or ad ID. If the ID type is unknown, ask where the user copied it from or request the Ads Manager URL instead of guessing. Calling it an "A/B test ID" does not establish the ID type. Use `ads_experiment_list_tests` with `ad_account_id` or `ad_entity_id` once the object type is known.

action.description: The action to perform. Supported: "cancel" (stops test, no results preserved), "end_test_now" (ends test immediately, results are preserved), "update" (edit test name or end date).

reason.description: Cancel reason. If not provided, defaults to "Canceled via MCP".

test_name.description: New test name. Only used with "update" action.

start_time.description: New start date as a YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. "2030-01-15"), not a Unix timestamp or date-time. It is interpreted at midnight in the ad account timezone and can only be changed before the test starts. Only used with "update" action.

end_time.description: New end date as a YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. "2030-01-22"), not a Unix timestamp or date-time. It is interpreted at midnight in the ad account timezone. Only used with "update" action.

tools.title: Experiment check eligibility
tools.description:
**CRITICAL TRIGGER:** Call this tool whenever a user asks about measuring incrementality, incremental conversions, causal impact, or if their ads can run an A/B test or Lift study. ALWAYS call this tool to verify account eligibility before attempting to create a new experiment.

 **CAPABILITIES:** Evaluates an ad account (or specific entities) to determine eligibility for both A/B tests (split tests) and Lift studies. Returns available test types, warnings, and recommendations.

 **RESPONSE RULES & STRATEGIC PITCH:**
 1. **SUMMARIZE:** Clearly report which test types the account is eligible for, surface any existing-study warnings, and provide the recommended path.
 2. **ADVOCATE FOR LIFT:** If the account is eligible for a Lift study, strongly encourage it. Shortened; describing this tool returns Meta's full guidance.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID (e.g. "act_123456789").

ad_entity_ids.description: Optional list of ad entity IDs (campaign, ad set, or ad IDs) to check eligibility for. When omitted, A/B test eligibility is skipped and Lift eligibility is evaluated against the ad account with the top 10 active campaigns by spend auto-discovered for campaign-level analysis.
